We've been listening to your feedback and we've got some exciting news!

notes.title: Patch #2 for Kusan: City of Wolves is now live, alongside a major update to the free Steam demo! 🛠️

items.text: This update brings some significant improvements to your journey through Kusan, including two difficulty modes, Floor Select, improved progression, combat balancing and quality-of-life updates.
And for anyone who hasn't experienced Kusan yet, we've expanded the demo with more playable content and the ability to carry your progress into the full game!
Whether you're a newcomer finding your feet or a seasoned Fixer chasing that perfect run, there's plenty to get your hands on.

notes.title: 🎮 Choose Your Challenge: Standard or Hard

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41028530/55ef63559d471de2de80c4209afdea64504d6b04.jpg"]
Kusan is a dangerous city, but now you can choose how you want to face it!
A more approachable way to experience Kusan's intense, fast-paced action.
More time to react: Enemies attack more slowly, giving you extra opportunities to dodge, counter and survive.
More ammunition: Improved ammo drops from several enemies and destructible objects help keep you in the fight.
Rebalanced encounters: Adjusted enemy placements and attack patterns across the campaign.
Hoban Convoy adjustments: Your attacks now deal increased damage to the convoy.
For Fixers looking for a tougher challenge!
Hard Mode retains the more demanding combat experience, with faster enemy attacks, tougher encounter layouts and more limited ammunition opportunities.
We've also made balancing adjustments to selected enemies and encounters to refine the challenge.
You can now switch difficulty directly from the Pause Menu. Changing modes will restart your current floor.
If you're struggling in Hard Mode, you'll also be offered the option to switch to Standard after repeated Game Overs.
Please note: Existing saves created before difficulty modes were introduced will initially use Hard Mode.

notes.title: 🗺️ Floor Select: Your Fight, Your Way!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41028530/eb2819fdbc58a8ce65554cea8e7d441d3fcda753.gif"]
Want another shot at a particular encounter?
Chasing a better grade?
Or just fancy replaying your favourite section?
You can now select previously unlocked starting points within stages, giving you greater freedom over how you tackle Kusan.
Replay unlocked floors without starting the entire stage again.
Unlock new starting points as you progress.
Switch between Standard and Hard from the Stage Select screen.
Earn grades and rewards based on the floors you complete.
We've also refined the way stage grades are displayed, making it easier to track your best performances.
Getting back into the action just got easier!
Previously, selecting Continue would start you at the beginning of the stage following your last completed stage.
Now, Continue takes you back to the last floor you entered, using the difficulty mode you were playing at the time.
That means less time retracing your steps and more time getting straight back into the action.
Older saves without a recorded floor entry will initially use the previous Continue behaviour.
We've made several adjustments to improve the feel, responsiveness and clarity of combat.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41028530/e0e1b5a8689eec741215d4ab71f801db3fd4e433.gif"]
Jin now prioritises enemies directly in front of his aiming direction when punching, helping you connect with your intended target more consistently.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41028530/0f1e1f1b77c9557b8a9b2bfe5ca80b6a94213e7f.jpg"]
The motorcycle sequences in Chapter 2-7 have received some extra attention.
Improved dash targeting when using keyboard controls.
Added crash effects and sounds when colliding with vehicles.
Side collisions with certain vehicles and trailers now block your movement instead of instantly defeating you.
Improved door physics and interactions.
Launched doors now break when hitting vehicles.
New visual trails make launching doors and walls more satisfying.
Certain event walls can no longer be destroyed before their encounters are complete.
We've made a few changes to improve the flow of Limbus challenges.
Most timed button-pattern challenges now give you eight seconds to complete their inputs.
Limbus Cores now begin moving towards Jin sooner and travel faster, making collection more convenient.
Both improvements apply across Standard and Hard modes.
It's not just the big features getting attention. We've also introduced several smaller improvements to make your time in Kusan smoother.
More keyboard, mouse and controller inputs can now skip the score animation after clearing a floor.
Selecting Main Menu or Quit now displays a confirmation prompt to help prevent accidental exits.
We've improved the tutorial's visual guidance and wording.
Selecting Don't Show Again will now correctly prevent the tutorial from appearing again.
Restored the original colours of several environmental objects.
Added new interface text for the difficulty modes.
Updated localisation and tutorial wording.
Improved how stage grades and progression are displayed.

notes.title: 🆕 The Kusan Demo Just Got Bigger!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41028530/d367151a3b916ee9277977dcea87da3a51843e57.png"]
Haven't played Kusan: City of Wolves yet?
Now's the perfect time to jump in!
Alongside Patch #2, we've released a major update to the free Steam demo, giving new players even more of Jin's journey to experience.
The demo now lets you play all the way through Stage 1-2!
Whether you're discovering Kusan for the first time or returning for another round, there's more action waiting for you.
The updated demo includes both Standard and Hard difficulty modes, so you can choose the challenge that suits your playstyle.
The demo also includes the latest gameplay improvements from the full game, including the changes introduced in Patch #2.
That means you can experience the updated combat, progression and quality-of-life features before committing to the full adventure.
Your demo save data is now compatible with the full game!
Enjoyed your time in the demo?
You can continue Jin's journey without having to start all over again.
We've also updated the demo's ending message to remind players that their adventure doesn't have to stop there.

notes.title: Alongside the headline changes, Patch #2 also includes

items.text: Adjustments to enemy attack timings and behaviour in Hard Mode.
Further balancing of the Hoban Convoy encounter.
Difficulty-specific enemy placements across 55 floors.
Additional differences in selected enemy encounters and NPC dialogue.
Ammunition drop adjustments in selected areas.
Improved score calculations when starting from later floors.
Refinements to stage grades and reward calculations.
Updated Korean main menu terminology.
These changes aim to make the overall experience smoother while preserving the fast, demanding combat at the heart of Kusan.
A huge thank you to everyone who's been playing Kusan: City of Wolves, trying the demo and sharing their experiences with us.
Your feedback continues to help the team identify areas for improvement, and these updates represent another step towards making Kusan even better.
Whether you're returning to improve your ranking or stepping into the city for the first time, we hope you enjoy everything this update has to offer.
We're continuing to listen, refine and improve the game, so please keep your feedback coming!
If you encounter any issues, please report them through our Bug Reports & Technical Support discussion board.
Hey Fixers, Wolves and Wild Punks!
Patch #1 for Kusan: City of Wolves is now live!
Since launch, we’ve been listening closely to your feedback and continuing to look at ways we can improve your journey through the streets of the city.

Patch #1 brings together a range of gameplay improvements, balancing changes and quality-of-life additions, including seeing further ahead, changes to Limbus Cores, improvements to boss encounters, new combat notifications, updated music arrangements and more.
We’ve added the ability to look further ahead within each floor, pressing SHIFT gives you a better view of what’s waiting beyond your immediate surroundings.
A new tutorial has also been added to introduce the feature.
We’ve made several changes to Limbus progression based on player feedback:
• A Limbus Clear Mark has been added to Chapter Select, making it easier to see which Limbus challenges you’ve already completed.
• Fixed an issue where players could run out of Limbus Cores before unlocking every available upgrade.
• Players can now earn Limbus Cores from previously cleared Limbus challenges, giving you another opportunity to earn the Cores needed to complete your upgrades.

notes.title: We’ve made several adjustments across combat encounters

items.text: • Added a notification before gun-wielding enemies fire, giving you a clearer opportunity to react.
• Rebalanced the slowdown AOE attacks used by the Cyborg Dog and Monkey enemies.
• Balanced the bullet patterns during the Stage 2-7 Hoban van fight.
• Increased boss damage from the Crossbow Charge Shot and Revolver Golden Bullet, making these powerful attacks even more effective against bosses.
Timing is everything.
We’ve added a new Parry sub-tutorial to Stage 2-1 and the Stage 2-7 boss fight, giving players additional guidance on one of Jin’s most important combat techniques.
We’ve made further refinements to the game’s music arrangement, improving how tracks are used throughout your journey and how the soundtrack complements the action.
Prefer a steadier view of the action?
A new Screen Shake option has been added, giving you greater control over how much screen movement you experience during combat.
We’ve also made visual improvements to the Final Boss fight, adding further polish to the climactic encounter awaiting Jin at the end of his journey.
We won’t spoil anything else. You’ll have to get there yourself.

notes.title: For a quick overview, here’s everything included in Patch 1

items.text: • Added the ability to look further ahead within floors, including a new tutorial.
• Updated and rearranged music throughout the game.
• Added a Limbus Clear Mark to Chapter Select.
• Fixed an issue where players could run out of Limbus Cores before unlocking all upgrades.
• Limbus Cores can now be earned from previously cleared Limbus challenges.
• Added visual improvements to the Final Boss fight.
• Added a notification before gun-wielding enemies fire.
• Rebalanced the Cyborg Dog and Monkey slowdown AOE attacks.
• Added a Screen Shake option.
• Balanced bullet patterns during the Stage 2-7 Hoban van fight.
• Increased boss damage from the Crossbow Charge Shot and Revolver Golden Bullet.
• Added a Parry sub-tutorial to Stage 2-1 and the Stage 2-7 boss fight.
Thank you to everyone who has been playing Kusan: City of Wolves and taking the time to share feedback with us.
Your reports and suggestions continue to help the team identify areas where we can improve the experience and we’ll keep listening as we continue supporting the game.
If you encounter a bug or technical issue, please let us know through the Bug Reports & Technical Support section of the Steam Discussions.
Now get back out there, Fixers.

Oh, one more thing...
We’re also preparing to launch a Public Playtest, giving you the opportunity to get hands-on with upcoming changes and actively participate in helping us improve Kusan: City of Wolves.
We’ll share more details on how you can take part soon, so keep an eye on the Steam Community for further updates.
Hello everyone,
Thank you again to everyone who completed the Kusan: City of Wolves playtest survey. We sincerely appreciate your interest and support.

We apologize for the delayed update, and for not communicating sooner. While we had originally hoped to move forward with the playtest last year, we decided to take additional time to further polish the game so we could present it in a stronger state and gather more meaningful feedback.

The review process has also taken longer than expected, and we are now in the final stage of reviewing applications. We will be contacting selected playtest participants soon with further details and next steps.
Even if you are not included in this round, we are very grateful for your support, and we expect to have more opportunities to participate as we move closer to launch.
